words.tr: adj. 受欢呼的；受赞誉的； v. “acclaim”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The acclaimed actor received a standing ovation.
words.ex_cn: 这位受欢呼的演员赢得了起立鼓掌。
words.en: Publicly praised; celebrated.

words.ex: The hotel provided free accommodations for the guests.
words.ex_cn: 酒店为客人提供了免费的住处。
words.en: Accommodations refer to a place where someone can stay, live, or work, especially a room, building, or other place that provides shelter or lodging.

words.ex: The accumulation of snow made the road dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 积雪使道路变得危险。
words.en: The process by which something increases in amount or is collected together over time.

words.ex: He finally acknowledged his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
words.en: If you acknowledge a fact or a situation, you accept or admit that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: The ticket is your admission to the concert.
words.ex_cn: 这张票是进入音乐会的许可。
words.en: An admission is a statement in which you admit that something bad, unpleasant, or embarrassing is true, or the act of allowing someone to enter a place or organization.

words.ex: The affluent family bought a big house by the lake.
words.ex_cn: 这个富裕的家庭在湖边买了一栋大房子。
words.en: Having a great deal of money; wealthy.

words.ex: The children are of different ages.
words.ex_cn: 这些孩子的年龄不同。
words.en: Ages refers to a very long time or the period of history that is being referred to.

words.ex: He shouted aggressively at the other driver.
words.ex_cn: 他挑衅地对另一名司机大喊。
words.en: If you do something aggressively, you do it in a forceful and determined way.

words.ex: He denied the allegation of stealing money.
words.ex_cn: 他否认了偷钱的指控。
words.en: An allegation is a statement saying that someone has done something wrong or illegal.

words.ex: The teacher will allocate books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将给学生分配书籍。
words.en: To allocate something means to give it to a particular person or use it for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The alteration of the dress made it fit better.
words.ex_cn: 这件衣服的修改让它更合身了。
words.en: An alteration is a change in or to something.

words.tr:
adj. 交替的；轮流的；间隔的；
v. （使）交替；（使）轮流；
words.ex: We take alternate days off work.
words.ex_cn: 我们隔天休息一次。
words.en: If something alternates between two things, it repeatedly changes from one to the other and back again.

words.tr: n. 替代选择；替代选择（alternative 的复数）；
words.ex: We need to find better alternatives to plastic.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要找到比塑料更好的替代选择。
words.en: An alternative is something that you can choose to do or use instead of something else.

words.ex: He uses aluminum foil to wrap the food.
words.ex_cn: 他用铝箔纸包食物。
words.en: A light, silvery metal that is used especially for making cooking equipment and aircraft parts.

words.ex: He is an ambassador to France.
words.ex_cn: 他是驻法国的大使。
words.en: An ambassador is an official envoy, especially a high-ranking diplomat who represents a state and is usually accredited to another sovereign state or to an international organization as the resident representative of their own government or sovereign or appointed for a special and often temporary diplomatic assignment.

words.tr: n. 歧义( ambiguity的名词复数 ); 意义不明确; 模棱两可的意思; 模棱两可的话
words.ex: The instructions have many ambiguities.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明有很多歧义。
words.en: Ambiguities refer to the quality of being open to more than one interpretation; inexactness.

words.ex: The sentence has ambiguity because it can mean two things.
words.ex_cn: 这句话有歧义，因为它可以有两种意思。
words.en: If you say that there is ambiguity in something, you mean that it is unclear or confusing, or it can be understood in more than one way.

words.ex: He is an ambitious student who wants to become a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有雄心的学生，想成为一名医生。
words.en: Having or showing a strong desire and determination to succeed.

words.ex: The amendment changed the old law.
words.ex_cn: 这项修正案改变了旧法律。
words.en: An amendment is a change or addition to a law or document.

words.ex: There is ample food for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都有足够的食物。
words.en: If there is an ample amount of something, there is enough of it and usually some extra.

words.ex: The amplifier gives amplification to the sound.
words.ex_cn: 放大器对声音进行放大。
words.en: The process of increasing the volume, extent, or significance of something.

words.ex: The two situations are analogous.
words.ex_cn: 这两种情况是相似的。
words.en: If one thing is analogous to another, the two things are similar in some way.

words.ex: He analyzes data every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天分析数据。
words.en: To examine something methodically and in detail, typically in order to explain and interpret it.

words.ex: My son loves watching cartoon animation.
words.ex_cn: 我儿子喜欢看卡通动画。
words.en: Animation is the process of making films in which drawings or puppets appear to move.

words.tr: adv. 不具名地；化名地；匿名地
words.ex: He posted the comment anonymously.
words.ex_cn: 他匿名发布了这条评论。
words.en: If something is done anonymously, it is done without the name of the person involved being known or made public.

words.ex: He has an appetite for spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢辛辣食物。
words.en: A desire or liking for something, especially food.

words.ex: The teacher chose an arbitrary number to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 老师随意选了一个数字来开始游戏。
words.en: If you describe an action, rule, or decision as arbitrary, you think that it is not based on any principle, plan, or system. It often seems unfair because of this.

words.ex: The archaeologist found an old pot in the ground.
words.ex_cn: 这位考古学家在地下发现了一个旧陶罐。
words.en: An archaeologist is someone who studies the societies and cultures of the past by examining the remains of their buildings, tools, and other objects.

words.ex: He studies architecture at university.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学学习建筑学。
words.en: Architecture is the art and science of designing buildings and other physical structures.

words.ex: The arid land has little rain and no trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片干旱的土地降雨稀少，没有树木。
words.en: An arid area of land has so little rain that it is very dry and cannot support much vegetation.

words.ex: The police arrested the thief last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚逮捕了那个小偷。
words.en: If the police arrest you, they take charge of you and take you to a police station, because they believe you may have committed a crime.

words.ex: He gave me his assurance that the work would be done on time.
words.ex_cn: 他向我保证工作会按时完成。
words.en: If you give someone an assurance that something is true or will happen, you say that it is definitely true or will definitely happen, in order to make them feel less worried.

words.tr: adj. 运动的；身强力壮的；
words.ex: He is an athletic boy who loves running.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个热爱跑步的运动型男孩。
words.en: Athletic is used to describe someone who is physically strong, fit, and good at sports, or something related to sports or physical activities.

words.ex: The goal is attainable if you work hard.
words.ex_cn: 如果你努力工作，这个目标是可以达到的。
words.en: If something is attainable, it is possible to achieve it.

words.ex: The children found old toys in the attic.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在阁楼上找到了旧玩具。
words.en: An attic is a space or room just below the roof of a building, often used for storage or as an extra room.

words.tr: n. 律师；辩护律师；代理人
words.ex: The attorney helped the man with his case.
words.ex_cn: 律师帮助那个人处理了他的案件。
words.en: An attorney is a lawyer who is qualified to represent a client in court.

words.ex: The old painting was sold at an auction.
words.ex_cn: 那幅旧画在拍卖会上被卖出了。
words.en: An auction is a public sale where goods or property are sold to the highest bidder.

words.ex: The manager will authorize the payment tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 经理明天将批准这笔付款。
words.en: To give official permission for something to happen, or to give someone official permission to do something.

words.tr: n. <戏>背景幕布( backdrop的名词复数 ); 周围的景物
words.ex: The painting has colorful backdrops.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有彩色的背景。
words.en: A backdrop is a large piece of cloth, often with scenery or buildings painted on it, that is hung at the back of a stage in a theatre. It can also refer to the setting or background against which something is viewed or takes place.

words.tr:
v. 打嗝；冒出
n. 嗝
words.ex: He belched after eating the big meal.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完这顿大餐后打了个嗝。
words.en: To expel gas noisily from the stomach through the mouth; to emit or discharge something forcefully.

words.tr: adj. 有偏见的； v. “bias”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The judge was biased against the defendant.
words.ex_cn: 这位法官对被告有偏见。
words.en: If someone is biased, they prefer one group of people to another, and behave unfairly as a result.

words.ex: He got a blister on his foot from new shoes.
words.ex_cn: 他新鞋磨出了一个水泡。
words.en: A blister is a small pocket of fluid within the upper layers of the skin, typically caused by forceful rubbing, burning, freezing, chemical exposure or infection. As a verb, it means to form such a pocket of fluid.

words.ex: He writes a blog about travel.
words.ex_cn: 他写一个关于旅行的博客。
words.en: A blog is a website containing a writer's or group of writers' own experiences, observations, opinions, etc., and often having images and links to other websites.

words.ex: The view from the mountain is breathtaking.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色令人惊叹。
words.en: If you say that something is breathtaking, you mean that it is extremely beautiful or amazing.

words.ex: He tried to bribe the officer with money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用钱贿赂官员。
words.en: A bribe is a sum of money or something valuable that one person offers or gives to another in order to persuade them to do something, usually something dishonest.

words.ex: She played the piano brilliantly.
words.ex_cn: 她出色地弹奏了钢琴。
words.en: In a way that is very impressive or excellent.

words.ex: The country is on the brink of war.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正处于战争的边缘。
words.en: If you are on the brink of something, you are about to do it or experience it.

words.ex: He uses Chrome as his browser.
words.ex_cn: 他用 Chrome 作为他的浏览器。
words.en: A browser is a piece of computer software that you use to search for information on the Internet.

words.tr: v. 擦伤；挫伤；出现伤痕；
words.ex: He bruised his knee when he fell off the bike.
words.ex_cn: 他从自行车上摔下来时擦伤了膝盖。
words.en: A bruise is a mark that appears on your skin after you have been injured, but the skin is not broken.

words.tr: n. 捆；捆( bundle的名词复数 )；
words.ex: He carried bundles of firewood to the house.
words.ex_cn: 他提着一捆捆木柴到房子那里。
words.en: A bundle is a number of things that are tied or wrapped together so that they can be carried or stored.

words.ex: He kept the dishes in the cabinet.
words.ex_cn: 他把盘子放在储藏柜里。
words.en: A cabinet is a piece of furniture with doors and shelves or drawers, used for storing or showing things. In politics, a cabinet is a group of people who are chosen by a head of state to give advice and to help set government policy.

words.ex: He uses a calculator to add numbers.
words.ex_cn: 他用计算器来加数字。
words.en: A calculator is a small electronic device that you use for doing mathematical calculations.

words.ex: The boat travels through the canal.
words.ex_cn: 船通过运河航行。
words.en: A canal is a long, narrow stretch of water that has been made for boats to travel along or to bring water to a particular area.

words.ex: He has the capacity to solve hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有能力解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: The capacity of a place or container is the amount of things or people that it can hold.

words.ex: He does cardio every morning to stay fit.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上做有氧运动来保持健康。
words.en: Cardio is a type of exercise that raises your heart rate, such as running, cycling, or swimming, and is especially good for your heart and lungs.

words.ex: She baked a chicken casserole for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她为晚餐烤了一道鸡肉砂锅菜。
words.en: A casserole is a dish consisting of a mixture of foods baked together in the oven.

words.ex: He was cautious when crossing the busy street.
words.ex_cn: 他过繁忙的街道时很小心。
words.en: If you are cautious, you are careful and avoid taking risks.

words.ex: The old cemetery is near the church.
words.ex_cn: 那个古老的墓地在教堂附近。
words.en: A cemetery is a place where dead people are buried.

words.ex: The chancellor announced a new tax policy.
words.ex_cn: 大臣宣布了一项新的税收政策。
words.en: A chancellor is the head of the government in some countries, or a high-ranking official in a university or other institution.

words.tr:
n. 特点；特性；
adj. 典型的；特有的；
words.ex: Honesty is a key characteristic of a good friend.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一个好朋友的关键特点。
words.en: A characteristic is a quality or feature that is typical of someone or something.

words.ex: His charisma made everyone want to follow him.
words.ex_cn: 他的超凡魅力让所有人都想追随他。
words.en: Charisma is a compelling attractiveness or charm that can inspire devotion in others.

words.ex: The choir sings every Sunday in church.
words.ex_cn: 唱诗班每周日在教堂唱歌。
words.en: A choir is a group of people who sing together, especially in a church or school.

words.ex: He eats eggs but watches his cholesterol.
words.ex_cn: 他吃鸡蛋，但注意自己的胆固醇。
words.en: Cholesterol is a substance that exists in the cells of the body and in blood, which can cause heart disease if there is too much of it.

words.tr:
n. 编年史；年代记
v. 按时间顺序记录
words.ex: He writes a chronicle of his daily life.
words.ex_cn: 他记录自己每天的生活。
words.en: A chronicle is a historical account of events arranged in chronological order, typically without analysis or interpretation.

words.tr: v. 将（某事物）载入编年史( chronicle的过去式和过去分词 )
words.ex: He chronicled his journey in a diary.
words.ex_cn: 他用日记记录了自己的旅程。
words.en: To chronicle something means to record events in the order in which they happened.

words.ex: The movie plot was cliched and predictable.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的情节陈词滥调且可预测。
words.en: A clichéd phrase, idea, or work of art is one that has been used so often that it is no longer original or interesting.

words.ex: The doctor gave him a clinical exam.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他做了临床检查。
words.en: Clinical means involving or relating to the direct observation and treatment of patients, rather than theoretical or laboratory studies.

words.tr: n. （有共同特点或举止类同的）一群人；一批人；
words.ex: The cohort of students all started college in 2020.
words.ex_cn: 这群学生都是在2020年进入大学的。
words.en: A cohort is a group of people who share a common characteristic or experience.

words.ex: His opinion coincides with mine.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点与我的一致。
words.en: If one event coincides with another, they happen at the same time.

words.ex: It's a coincidence that we both wore blue today.
words.ex_cn: 我们今天都穿了蓝色，真是巧合。
words.en: A coincidence is when two or more similar or related events occur at the same time by chance and without any planning.

words.ex: They collaborate to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他们合作完成这个项目。
words.en: to work jointly with others or together especially in an intellectual endeavor

words.ex: He learned good collocation from his English teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他从英语老师那里学到了好的词语搭配。
words.en: The habitual juxtaposition of a particular word with another word or words with a frequency greater than chance.

words.tr: n. 舒适；给予援助或安慰的人或事；安慰( comfort的名词复数 )；
words.ex: The soft blanket and warm tea brought her many comforts.
words.ex_cn: 柔软的毯子和热茶给她带来了许多舒适。
words.en: Things that make life more pleasant or easier, especially in terms of physical well-being.

words.ex: The commander gave the order to advance.
words.ex_cn: 指挥官下达了前进的命令。
words.en: A commander is a person in authority, especially in the armed forces, who gives orders and is responsible for the actions of those under their command.

words.tr: adj. 有同情心的；表示怜悯的；
words.ex: She is a compassionate teacher who helps struggling students.
words.ex_cn: 她是一位有同情心的老师，帮助学习困难的学生。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as compassionate, you mean that they feel or show pity, sympathy, and understanding for people who are suffering.

words.ex: The law compels drivers to wear seat belts.
words.ex_cn: 法律强迫司机系安全带。
words.en: If a situation, a rule, or a person compels you to do something, they force you to do it.

words.ex: He is a competent teacher who helps students easily.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有能力的老师，能轻松帮助学生。
words.en: If you are competent to do something, you have the skills, abilities, or experience necessary to do it well.

words.ex: The completion of the project took three months.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的完成花了三个月。
words.en: The act of finishing or making something whole or perfect.

words.ex: Too many rules can complicate the game.
words.ex_cn: 太多的规则会使游戏变得复杂。
words.en: To make something more difficult to understand or deal with by adding more parts or details.

words.ex: The math problem is complicated.
words.ex_cn: 这个数学问题很复杂。
words.en: Involving many different and confusing aspects.

words.tr:
v. 称赞；恭维
n. 称赞；恭维
words.ex: He gave her a compliment on her dress.
words.ex_cn: 他夸了她的裙子。
words.en: A compliment is a polite expression of praise or admiration.

words.ex: A car has many components, like wheels and engines.
words.ex_cn: 汽车有许多部分，比如轮子和发动机。
words.en: A component is a part of a larger whole, especially a part that can be separated from or attached to a system.

words.ex: The team comprises five players and one coach.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队包括五名球员和一名教练。
words.en: If you say that something comprises or is comprised of a number of things or people, you mean it has them as its parts or members.

words.tr: adj. 自负的；骄傲自大的
words.ex: He is conceited because he thinks he is the smartest.
words.ex_cn: 他自以为是，因为他觉得自己最聪明。
words.en: If you say that someone is conceited, you are showing your disapproval of the fact that they are far too proud of their abilities or achievements.

words.tr: v. 设想；构想；怀孕；想出；想出( conceive的过去式和过去分词 )；
words.ex: He conceived a new plan to save money.
words.ex_cn: 他设想了一个新的省钱计划。
words.en: To conceive means to form or devise a plan or idea in the mind, or to become pregnant.

words.tr:
n. 混凝土；
adj. 具体的；
words.ex: The workers poured concrete to build the foundation.
words.ex_cn: 工人们浇筑混凝土来建造地基。
words.en: Concrete is a hard, strong construction material made by mixing a cementing material (such as Portland cement) and a mineral aggregate (such as sand and gravel) with sufficient water to cause the cement to set and bind the entire mass. In a broader sense, concrete can also refer to something that is tangible, specific, or real.

words.ex: The document is confidential and cannot be shared.
words.ex_cn: 这份文件是机密的，不能分享。
words.en: If you talk to someone in a confidential way, you talk to them quietly because what you are saying is secret or private.

words.ex: He must confront his fears.
words.ex_cn: 他必须面对自己的恐惧。
words.en: If you confront a difficult situation or issue, you accept the fact that it exists and try to deal with it.

words.ex: The confrontation between the two teams was intense.
words.ex_cn: 两队之间的对抗非常激烈。
words.en: A confrontation is a situation in which there is a lot of disagreement or argument about something important.

words.ex: Traffic congestion caused delays on the highway.
words.ex_cn: 交通堵塞导致了高速公路的延误。
words.en: Congestion refers to the state of being overcrowded, especially with traffic or people, or the condition of being blocked or clogged.

words.ex: The team reached a consensus on the project plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队就项目计划达成了共识。
words.en: A consensus is general agreement among a group of people.

words.ex: He is a conservative man who likes old traditions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢古老传统的保守男子。
words.en: A conservative person or group is one that does not like changes or new ideas, especially in politics or religion.

words.tr: adv. 大幅度地；相当地；很大地；
words.ex: The price has increased considerably.
words.ex_cn: 价格大幅上涨了。
words.en: To a notably large or significant extent.

words.tr: adj. 一致的；始终如一的；
words.ex: His answers are consistent with the data.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案与数据一致。
words.en: Someone who is consistent always behaves in the same way, has the same attitudes towards people or things, or achieves the same level of success in something.

words.ex: The letter 'b' is a consonant.
words.ex_cn: 字母 'b' 是一个辅音。
words.en: A consonant is a speech sound that is articulated with complete or partial closure of the vocal tract.

words.ex: The constitution protects the rights of all citizens.
words.ex_cn: 宪法保护所有公民的权利。
words.en: The constitution of a country or organization is the system of laws which formally states people's rights and duties.

words.tr: v. 考虑；深思；凝视；思考…的可能性
words.ex: He contemplates quitting his job.
words.ex_cn: 他正在考虑辞去工作。
words.en: If you contemplate an action, you think about whether to do it or not.

words.tr: v. 竞争；争夺；争辩；辩驳；“contest”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The election result was contested by the loser.
words.ex_cn: 选举结果被失败者质疑。
words.en: If something is contested, it is the subject of a dispute or competition.

words.tr: adj. 欧洲大陆的；大陆的；
words.ex: He prefers continental breakfast with bread and coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他更喜欢欧洲大陆式的早餐，有面包和咖啡。
words.en: Continental is used to describe something that relates to or is characteristic of a continent, especially the mainland of Europe as distinct from the British Isles.

words.ex: He uses contraception to avoid having a baby.
words.ex_cn: 他使用避孕措施来避免怀孕。
words.en: Contraception is the use of methods or devices to prevent pregnancy.

words.ex: His words are a contradiction.
words.ex_cn: 他的话是矛盾的。
words.en: A contradiction is a situation or statement in which two aspects or elements are opposed to each other, making it impossible for both to be true at the same time.

words.ex: His words were contradictory.
words.ex_cn: 他的话是矛盾的。
words.en: If two or more facts, ideas, or statements are contradictory, they state or imply that opposite things are true.

words.ex: It is a convention to shake hands when you meet someone.
words.ex_cn: 见面时握手是一种习俗。
words.en: A convention is a large meeting of an organization or political group, or a way of behaving that is considered to be correct or polite by most people in a society.

words.tr:
adj. 合作的；
n. 合作社；
words.ex: The two companies made a cooperative effort to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 两家公司合作努力解决问题。
words.en: A cooperative is an organization or business that is owned and run jointly by its members, who share the profits or benefits.

words.tr: n. 必然的结果（或结论）；推论
words.ex: The theorem leads to a simple corollary.
words.ex_cn: 这个定理引出了一个简单的推论。
words.en: A corollary is a statement that follows on from another statement, and that is usually easily understood or proved.

words.ex: The boy walked down the long corridor.
words.ex_cn: 男孩走过了长长的走廊。
words.en: A corridor is a long passage in a building, with doors and rooms on one or both sides.

words.tr: adj. 全世界的；四海一家的；
words.ex: This city has a cosmopolitan population.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市有着来自世界各地的人口。
words.en: A cosmopolitan place or society is full of people from many different countries and cultures.

words.tr: n. 理事会；委员会；议会；
words.ex: The city council made a new rule about recycling.
words.ex_cn: 市政府理事会制定了关于回收的新规定。
words.en: A council is a group of people who are elected to govern a local area such as a city or, in Britain, a county.

words.ex: The cat creeps slowly toward the bird.
words.ex_cn: 猫蹑手蹑脚地向鸟靠近。
words.en: To move slowly and quietly, especially in a way that does not attract attention.

words.ex: The old wall began to crumble after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 旧墙在雨后开始坍塌。
words.en: If something crumbles, or if you crumble it, it breaks into a lot of small pieces.

words.tr:
adj. 狡猾的；奸诈的；巧妙的
n. 奸诈；狡猾
words.ex: The cunning fox tricked the chicken.
words.ex_cn: 那只狡猾的狐狸骗了鸡。
words.en: Someone who is cunning is clever and good at deceiving others in order to get what they want.

words.ex: The school changed its curriculum last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年学校更改了课程。
words.en: A curriculum is the subjects that are studied in a school, college, or university.

words.tr:
adj. 晕眩的；头昏的；迷糊的
v. 使发昏；使迷乱；“daze”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He stood dazed after the loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音后，他呆立着，晕头转向。
words.en: If someone is dazed, they are confused and unable to think clearly, often because of shock or a blow to the head.

words.tr:
v. 使目眩；使眼花；使惊叹
n. 耀眼；眩惑；灿烂
words.ex: The stars dazzle at night.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚的星星闪耀夺目。
words.en: If something dazzles you, it is so bright that you cannot see properly for a short time. It can also mean to greatly impress someone.

words.ex: He deceived his friend with a lie.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个谎言欺骗了朋友。
words.en: If you deceive someone, you make them believe something that is not true, usually in order to get some advantage for yourself.

words.ex: The deceptive smile hid his true intentions.
words.ex_cn: 那欺骗性的微笑隐藏了他真正的意图。
words.en: If something is deceptive, it encourages you to believe something which is not true.

words.tr: adj. 装饰性的；作装饰用的；
words.ex: The room has decorative flowers on the table.
words.ex_cn: 房间里桌上有一些装饰性的花。
words.en: Something that is decorative is intended to look pretty or attractive.

words.tr: adj. 专注的；专用的；献身的； v. 奉献；“dedicate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is dedicated to his studies.
words.ex_cn: 他专注于学习。
words.en: If you say that someone is dedicated to something, you approve of the fact that they have committed to it and are willing to give a lot of time and energy to it.

words.ex: His deficiency in math made him struggle in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学上的缺乏让他在课堂上很吃力。
words.en: A deficiency is a lack or shortage of something that is needed.

words.ex: The boy defied his parents by staying out late.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩因为熬夜不回家而违抗了父母。
words.en: If you defy someone or something, you refuse to obey them or you do something that they do not allow.

words.ex: The courier delivers packages every morning.
words.ex_cn: 快递员每天早上递送包裹。
words.en: To bring and hand over (a letter, parcel, or ordered goods) to the proper recipient or address; to give birth to a baby; to present or utter something in a formal or official manner.

words.ex: He votes in a democratic election.
words.ex_cn: 他在民主选举中投票。
words.en: A democratic country, government, or political system is governed by representatives who are elected by the people.

words.tr: n. 粗斜纹棉布；劳动布；牛仔布
words.ex: He wears blue denim jeans every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天穿蓝色牛仔裤。
words.en: Denim is a kind of cotton fabric, typically blue, used for making jeans, jackets, and other clothing.

words.ex: He uses deodorant every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都用除臭剂。
words.en: A deodorant is a substance that you can use on your body to prevent or mask the smell of sweat.

words.ex: He felt deep depression after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到深深的抑郁。
words.en: A period during which business, employment, and stock-market values decline severely or remain at a very low level of activity.

words.ex: The deputy signed the document for the manager.
words.ex_cn: 代理人替经理签署了文件。
words.en: A deputy is a person who is appointed to act as a substitute for another, especially in a position of authority.

words.ex: He is a descendant of the first king.
words.ex_cn: 他是第一位国王的后裔。
words.en: A person, plant, or animal that is descended from a particular ancestor.

words.tr: adj. 渴望的；想得到的； v. 渴望；“desire”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He got the desired job after months of searching.
words.ex_cn: 经过几个月的寻找，他得到了渴望的工作。
words.en: Wished for or wanted.

words.tr: adj. 不顾一切的；极度渴望的；绝望的；
words.ex: He made a desperate attempt to save the child.
words.ex_cn: 他不顾一切地试图救那个孩子。
words.en: If you are desperate, you are in such a bad situation that you are willing to try anything to change it.

words.ex: He called for help in desperation.
words.ex_cn: 他绝望地呼救。
words.en: Desperation is the feeling that you have when you are in such a bad situation that you are willing to take any risk to change it.

words.ex: The weather will deteriorate tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天天气会恶化。
words.en: If something deteriorates, it becomes worse in some way.

words.ex: The word 'this' is a determiner.
words.ex_cn: 单词 'this' 是一个限定词。
words.en: A determiner is a word that is used before a noun to show which particular example of the noun you are referring to.

words.tr: v. 毁灭；摧毁；“devastate”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 非常伤心的；
words.ex: The earthquake devastated the small town.
words.ex_cn: 地震摧毁了这个小镇。
words.en: If you are devastated by something, you are very shocked and upset by it. If a place is devastated, it is severely damaged or destroyed.

words.tr: adj. 毁灭性的； v. “devastate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The earthquake caused devastating damage to the city.
words.ex_cn: 地震对这座城市造成了毁灭性的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something as devastating, you are emphasizing that it is very harmful or damaging.

words.ex: The doctor can diagnose the illness quickly.
words.ex_cn: 医生能很快诊断出这种病。
words.en: If someone or something is diagnosed as having a particular illness or problem, their illness or problem is identified. If an illness or problem is diagnosed, it is identified.

words.ex: The old man walked with a dignified posture.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人以有尊严的姿态行走。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is dignified, you mean they are calm, impressive and deserve respect.

words.ex: He kept his dignity even when he was poor.
words.ex_cn: 即使他很穷，他依然保持尊严。
words.en: Dignity is the quality of being worthy of honor or respect.

words.ex: He faced a dilemma: stay home or go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他面临一个困境：是待在家里还是去上班。
words.en: A situation in which a difficult choice has to be made between two or more alternatives, especially equally undesirable ones.

words.ex: I looked up his phone number in the directory.
words.ex_cn: 我在姓名地址录里查了他的电话号码。
words.en: A directory is a book or list which gives names, addresses, and other information about people or organizations.

words.ex: The hard chair caused him discomfort.
words.ex_cn: 这把硬椅子让他感到不舒适。
words.en: Discomfort is a feeling of slight pain or physical unease, or a feeling of worry or embarrassment.

words.ex: The teacher gave students discretion to choose their own topic.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了学生自行选择题目的权利。
words.en: Discretion is the quality of behaving in a quiet and controlled way without drawing attention to yourself or giving away personal or private information.

words.ex: He noticed the discrimination between the two prices.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了两个价格之间的区别。
words.en: The unjust or prejudicial treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, age, or sex.

words.tr: adj. 不再抱幻想的； v. “disillusion”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He became disillusioned after seeing the truth.
words.ex_cn: 在看到真相后，他不再抱幻想了。
words.en: If you are disillusioned with something, you are disappointed because it is not as good as you had expected.

words.ex: He wrote his dissertation on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于气候变化的学位论文。
words.en: A dissertation is a long piece of writing on a particular subject, especially one written for a university degree.

words.tr: adj. 烦恼的； v. “distress”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: She looked distressed after hearing the bad news.
words.ex_cn: 听到坏消息后，她显得很烦恼。
words.en: If someone is distressed, they are extremely upset.

words.tr: adj. 令人苦恼的； v. “distress”的现在分词；
words.ex: The news was distressing for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个消息对每个人来说都是令人苦恼的。
words.en: Causing anxiety, sorrow or pain; upsetting.

words.ex: The school values diversity in its students.
words.ex_cn: 学校重视学生的多样性。
words.en: The state of being diverse; variety.

words.tr:
n. 纪录片；
adj. 文书的；
words.ex: We watched a documentary about pandas last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚看了一部关于熊猫的纪录片。
words.en: A documentary is a film or television or radio programme that gives factual information about a particular subject.

words.ex: He felt stuck in the doldrums after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到陷入低谷。
words.en: The doldrums are a state of inactivity or stagnation, especially in reference to a period of time or a geographical area known for its calm winds.

words.ex: He is an expert in the domain of artificial intelligence.
words.ex_cn: 他是人工智能领域的专家。
words.en: A domain is a particular field of thought, activity, or interest, especially one over which someone has control, influence, or rights.

words.ex: His dominance in the game surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中的支配表现让所有人感到惊讶。
words.en: Dominance is the state of being more powerful, important, or noticeable than other people or things.

words.ex: The dominant color in the room is blue.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间占优势的颜色是蓝色。
words.en: Someone or something that is dominant is more powerful, successful, influential, or noticeable than other people or things.

words.ex: The empire's domination over the region lasted for centuries.
words.ex_cn: 这个帝国对该地区的统治持续了几个世纪。
words.en: The exercise of control or influence over someone or something, or the state of being so controlled.

words.ex: The hospital received a donation of books.
words.ex_cn: 医院收到了一批书籍捐赠。
words.en: A donation is a gift which is given to a charity or other organization.

words.tr: n. 乱写乱画（出的东西）；乱写乱画（出的东西）( doodle的名词复数 ) v. 心不在焉地乱写乱画( doodle的；
words.ex: The child drew silly doodles on his notebook.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在他的笔记本上乱写乱画了一些傻乎乎的图案。
words.en: Doodles are simple drawings that are made without thinking too much or without trying to draw something specific.

words.ex: He has a dual role as teacher and coach.
words.ex_cn: 他同时担任老师和教练的双重角色。
words.en: Having two parts or aspects.

words.tr: adj. 可疑的；怀疑的；拿不准的；
words.ex: The deal seemed dubious to me.
words.ex_cn: 这个交易在我看来很可疑。
words.en: If you describe something as dubious, you mean that you do not consider it to be completely honest, safe, or reliable.

words.ex: The eagle flies high above the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 鹰在山上面高飞。
words.en: A large bird of prey with a massive hooked bill and long broad wings, known for its keen sight and powerful soaring flight.

words.ex: They live ecologically to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 他们以环保的方式生活以保护环境。
words.en: In a way that relates to ecology or the environment.

words.ex: He majors in economics at university.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学主修经济学。
words.en: Economics is the study of the way in which money, industry, and trade are organized in a society.

words.tr: adj. 可食用的；可以吃的；
words.ex: These mushrooms are edible and safe to eat.
words.ex_cn: 这些蘑菇是可食用的，安全可以吃。
words.en: Fit to be eaten as food.

words.tr:
adj. 精心制作的；详尽的；
v. 精心制作；详尽阐述；
words.ex: She wore an elaborate dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件精心制作的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: To elaborate means to add more details to something that has already been said or written, making it more complex or detailed. As an adjective, it describes something that is very complex and detailed.

words.tr: adj. 有资格的；合格的；合意的；
words.ex: He is eligible to vote because he is 18 years old.
words.ex_cn: 他年满18岁，有资格投票。
words.en: Someone who is eligible for something is qualified or allowed to do it.

words.ex: We must eliminate the waste to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须消除浪费以保护环境。
words.en: To eliminate something, especially something you do not want or need, means to remove it completely.

words.ex: The elite of the city often meet at private clubs.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的精英经常在私人俱乐部会面。
words.en: You can refer to the most powerful, rich, or talented people within a particular group, place, or society as the elite.

words.tr: adj. 难以捉摸的；不易被抓获（觉察、理解或记忆）的；
words.ex: The truth remained elusive.
words.ex_cn: 真相难以捉摸。
words.en: Difficult to find, catch, or achieve; difficult to remember or understand.

words.ex: The factory reduces emission to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 工厂减少排放以保护环境。
words.en: An emission is the production and discharge of something, especially gas or radiation.

words.ex: The coach endorses the new player.
words.ex_cn: 教练支持这位新球员。
words.en: If you endorse someone or something, you say publicly that you support or approve of them.

words.ex: He endow a library with books.
words.ex_cn: 他捐赠了一图书馆的书。
words.en: If someone is endowed with a particular quality or ability, they naturally have it.

words.ex: He had to endure the cold winter without a coat.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不在没有外套的情况下忍受寒冷的冬天。
words.en: To endure means to suffer something difficult, unpleasant, or painful, or to continue to exist for a long time.

words.tr: adj. 充满热情的；热心的；
words.ex: He is enthusiastic about playing basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他对打篮球充满热情。
words.en: If you are enthusiastic about something, you show how much you like or enjoy it by the way that you behave and talk.

words.tr: v. 授权；命名；给...权利（或资格）
words.ex: This book entitles you to a free gift.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使你有资格获得一份免费礼物。
words.en: If you are entitled to something, you have the right to have it or do it.

words.ex: The equation is easy to solve.
words.ex_cn: 这个方程式很容易解。
words.en: An equation is a mathematical statement that asserts the equality of two expressions.

words.tr:
n. 等价物；
adj. 相等的；等价的；
words.ex: The dollar is the equivalent of ten yuan.
words.ex_cn: 美元是十元的等价物。
words.en: If one amount or value is the equivalent of another, they are the same.

words.tr: n. 根除；连根拔除；消灭；
words.ex: The government aims at the eradication of poverty.
words.ex_cn: 政府的目标是根除贫困。
words.en: The complete destruction of something so that it no longer exists.

words.tr: v. 侵蚀；腐蚀；逐渐丧失；削弱
words.ex: The wind erodes the sand slowly.
words.ex_cn: 风慢慢侵蚀着沙子。
words.en: If rock or soil erodes or is eroded by the weather, sea, or wind, it cracks and breaks so that it is gradually destroyed.

words.tr: adv. 本质上；基本上；根本上；
words.ex: He is essentially a kind person.
words.ex_cn: 他本质上是个善良的人。
words.en: You use essentially to indicate that what you are saying is mainly true, although there may be some exceptions or qualifications.

words.tr: v. 估算；估价；“estimate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He estimated the cost of the trip.
words.ex_cn: 他估算了一下旅行的费用。
words.en: An estimated amount or quantity is one that is based on a guess or calculation, rather than on exact measurement.

words.tr: adv. 道德上地；伦理上地；
words.ex: He acted ethically when he returned the lost wallet.
words.ex_cn: 当他归还丢失的钱包时，他道德上地做了正确的事。
words.en: In a manner relating to moral principles or the branch of knowledge dealing with these.

words.ex: The festival celebrates ethnic music and dance.
words.ex_cn: 这个节日庆祝民族音乐和舞蹈。
words.en: Ethnic relates to a group of people who have a common national or cultural tradition.

words.ex: He exaggerates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸张自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you exaggerate, you indicate that something is, for example, worse or more important than it really is.

words.tr: adj. 卓越的；杰出的；罕见的；特别的；
words.ex: She is an exceptional student who always gets top grades.
words.ex_cn: 她是一名卓越的学生，总是取得最高分。
words.en: An exceptional person or thing has some unusual quality or ability that makes them different from others.

words.ex: He uses this park exclusively for walking.
words.ex_cn: 他只在这个公园散步。
words.en: If you do something exclusively, you do it only in the way mentioned, and not in any other way.

words.tr:
n. 决策人；行政官；管理人员；
adj. 行政的；决策的；
words.ex: The executive decided to launch the new product.
words.ex_cn: 这位决策人决定推出新产品。
words.en: An executive is a person who has a senior management position in a business or other organization.

words.ex: He exploited the situation to get more money.
words.ex_cn: 他利用这个情况赚了更多钱。
words.en: To exploit someone or something means to use them in a way that benefits you, often unfairly or without considering their rights or feelings. It can also refer to the act of making full use of and deriving benefit from a resource.

words.tr: adj. 精美的；细腻的；强烈的
words.ex: She wore an exquisite dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精美的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is exquisite is extremely beautiful or pleasant, especially in a delicate or refined way.

words.tr: adj. 广大的；广阔的；广泛的；大量的；
words.ex: He has extensive knowledge of history.
words.ex_cn: 他拥有广博的历史知识。
words.en: Something that is extensive covers a wide area or includes a lot of things.

words.ex: The external wall of the house is painted blue.
words.ex_cn: 房子的外墙被刷成了蓝色。
words.en: External is used to indicate that something is on the outside of a surface or body, or that it exists, happens, or comes from outside.

words.tr: adj. 灭绝的；熄灭的；绝种的；
words.ex: The dodo is an extinct bird.
words.ex_cn: 渡渡鸟是一种灭绝的鸟。
words.en: If a species of animals or plants is extinct, it no longer has any living members, either in the world or in a particular place.

words.tr:
v. 提取；
n. 摘录；提取物；
words.ex: They extract oil from plants.
words.ex_cn: 他们从植物中提取油。
words.en: To remove or take out something, especially by effort or force.

words.ex: He bought an extravagant car that cost too much money.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆奢侈的车，价格太贵了。
words.en: Spending much more than is necessary or wise; excessively expensive.

words.tr:
n. 极端主义者；过激分子
adj. 极端主义的；过激的
words.ex: The extremist refused to listen to others.
words.ex_cn: 这个极端分子拒绝倾听别人的意见。
words.en: An extremist is someone who has extreme political or religious ideas and is willing to do things that are illegal, violent, or not normal in order to achieve their aims.

words.tr: n. 织物；（建筑物的）结构；
words.ex: The dress is made of soft fabric.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子是由柔软的织物制成的。
words.en: Fabric refers to cloth or other material produced by weaving together cotton, nylon, wool, silk, or other threads. It can also refer to the basic structure of a building or a system.

words.ex: The concert was fabulous!
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会太棒了！
words.en: If you describe something as fabulous, you are emphasizing that you like it a lot or think that it is very good.

words.tr: v. 促进；使便利；使容易；
words.ex: The teacher facilitates learning by asking questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师通过提问来促进学习。
words.en: To make an action or process easier or more likely to happen.

words.ex: The faculty of engineering has many labs.
words.ex_cn: 工程学院有许多实验室。
words.en: A faculty is a group of departments in a university or college that specialize in a particular subject or group of subjects, or the teachers in such a group.

words.ex: The village suffered from famine last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年这个村庄遭受了饥荒。
words.en: A famine is a serious shortage of food in a country, which may cause many people to get sick or die.

words.ex: The movie was fantastically funny.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影极其搞笑。
words.en: In a manner that is extraordinarily good or attractive; in a way that is difficult to believe.

words.ex: It is feasible to finish the project in one week.
words.ex_cn: 一周内完成这个项目是可行的。
words.en: If something is feasible, it can be done, made, or achieved.

words.ex: The countries formed a federation to share resources.
words.ex_cn: 这些国家组成了一个联盟来共享资源。
words.en: A federation is a group of states or organizations that have joined together to form a single entity with a central government or authority.

words.tr:
adj. 假装的；不真实的
v. 假装；装作；“feign”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He feigned sleep to avoid talking.
words.ex_cn: 他假装睡觉以避免交谈。
words.en: If someone's behaviour or emotion is feigned, it is not genuine or sincere, but is pretended for effect.

words.ex: She has a feminine voice.
words.ex_cn: 她的声音很女性化。
words.en: having qualities or an appearance traditionally associated with women, especially delicacy and prettiness.

words.tr: adj. 肥沃的；有繁殖力的；多产的；富饶的；
words.ex: The fertile land grows many crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片肥沃的土地长满了各种作物。
words.en: Land or soil that is fertile is able to support the growth of a large number of strong healthy plants.

words.ex: The floor was filthy after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨过后，地板变得非常肮脏。
words.en: Something that is filthy is extremely dirty.

words.ex: The floppy ears of the dog waved when it ran.
words.ex_cn: 狗的松垂耳朵在它跑时晃动。
words.en: Something that is floppy is loose and soft, often hanging or bending in a way that suggests it lacks stiffness.

words.tr: v. 繁荣兴旺；茁壮成长；
words.ex: The business flourishes in the new market.
words.ex_cn: 这家企业在新市场中繁荣兴旺。
words.en: If something flourishes, it is successful, active, or common, and developing quickly and strongly.

words.tr: adj. 波动的； v. “fluctuate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The price of oil is fluctuating every day.
words.ex_cn: 石油的价格每天都在波动。
words.en: If something fluctuates, it changes a lot in an irregular way.

words.tr: adj. 禁止的；不许的； v. “forbid”的过去分词；
words.ex: The forbidden area is off-limits to visitors.
words.ex_cn: 这个禁止区域对游客关闭。
words.en: If something is forbidden, you are not allowed to do it or have it.

words.ex: The storm was formidable and destroyed many houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴很可怕，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as formidable, you mean that you feel slightly frightened by them because they are very great or impressive.

words.ex: He drew a fractal on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上画了一个分形。
words.en: A fractal is a complex geometric shape that can be split into parts, each of which is a reduced-scale copy of the whole, a property called self-similarity.

words.tr: adj. 成碎片的；片断的； v. “fragment”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The glass became fragmented after it fell.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃掉落后变成了碎片。
words.en: Something that is fragmented is broken into separate parts or pieces, often in a way that is confusing or makes it difficult to understand the whole.

words.ex: She was frantic to catch the last bus.
words.ex_cn: 她急忙赶着赶最后一班公交车。
words.en: If someone is frantic, they are behaving in a wild and desperate way, often because they are frightened or worried.

words.ex: The man was punished for fraud.
words.ex_cn: 这个人因欺骗而受到惩罚。
words.en: Fraud is the crime of gaining money or financial benefits by a trick or by lying.

words.ex: The company made fraudulent claims about its product.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司对其产品做出了欺诈性的声明。
words.en: A fraudulent activity is deceitful or dishonest.

words.ex: The town is near the frontier of the country.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇靠近国家的边境。
words.en: A frontier is a border between two countries or the area close to it. It can also refer to the limit of knowledge or the most advanced or recent stage in the development of something.

words.ex: The doctors are working on the frontlines.
words.ex_cn: 医生们正在前线工作。
words.en: The frontlines refer to the area where the most important work in a particular field is being done, especially in a war or conflict.

words.tr: adj. 基本的；基础的；根本的；
words.ex: Water is a fundamental need for life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命的基本需求。
words.en: You use fundamental to describe things, activities, and principles that are very important or essential. They affect the basic nature of other things or are the most important element upon which other things depend.

words.ex: He went to his grandfather's funeral.
words.ex_cn: 他去参加了他祖父的葬礼。
words.en: A funeral is a ceremony that is held because someone has died.

words.ex: He slammed the door furiously.
words.ex_cn: 他愤怒地摔上了门。
words.en: In a manner that is full of anger or energy; violently.

words.ex: He made a generalization from the data.
words.ex_cn: 他从数据中做出了一个概括。
words.en: A generalization is a statement that seems to be true in most situations or for most people, but that may not be completely true in all cases.

words.ex: He is a genius in math.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学方面是个天才。
words.en: Someone who is a genius is a person who is exceptionally intelligent or talented, especially in a particular field.

words.ex: She likes swimming, which is a gerund.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢游泳，这是一个动名词。
words.en: A gerund is a noun formed from a verb which refers to an action, process, or state. In English, gerunds end in -ing (e.g., 'swimming' in 'Swimming is good exercise.').

words.tr:
adj. 巨大的；伟大的；
n. 巨人；伟人；
words.ex: The giant elephant stood near the tree.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的大象站在树旁。
words.en: A giant is an imaginary person who is very big and strong, especially one mentioned in old stories. In everyday language, a giant can also refer to a very large and successful company or organization.

words.ex: Globalization helps countries trade more easily.
words.ex_cn: 全球化帮助各国更容易地进行贸易。
words.en: The process by which businesses or other organizations develop international influence or start operating on an international scale.

words.ex: The gossip about the CEO made everyone shocked.
words.ex_cn: 关于CEO的流言蜚语让所有人都震惊了。
words.en: Gossip is informal conversation or reports about other people's private lives, which might be unkind or not true.

words.tr:
n. 坟墓；
adj. 严重的；
words.ex: They visited the grave of their grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他们参观了祖父的坟墓。
words.en: A grave is a place where a dead person is buried. When used as an adjective, grave means serious or solemn.

words.ex: His greed made him steal money from his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他的贪婪让他偷了朋友的钱。
words.en: Greed is the desire to have more of something, such as food or money, than is necessary or fair.

words.ex: The policeman held a gun.
words.ex_cn: 警察拿着一把枪。
words.en: A gun is a weapon designed to discharge projectiles, often metal bullets, by the force of an explosive such as gunpowder.

words.tr: adj. 体操的；体操训练的
words.ex: He practices gymnastic routines every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上练习体操动作。
words.en: Relating to or involving gymnastics or physical exercises.

words.tr: adj. 手提式的，便携式的
words.ex: He uses a hand-held camera to take photos.
words.ex_cn: 他用手持相机拍照。
words.en: A hand-held device is a piece of electronic equipment that you can hold in your hands and use, such as a mobile phone or a tablet.

words.ex: He reported the harassment to the police.
words.ex_cn: 他向警察报告了骚扰行为。
words.en: Harassment is behaviour which is intended to trouble or annoy someone, especially repeated behaviour.

words.ex: He felt hatred for the man who hurt his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他憎恨那个伤害他兄弟的人。
words.en: Hatred is an extremely strong feeling of dislike for someone or something.

words.ex: The broken glass is a hazard.
words.ex_cn: 碎玻璃是危险。
words.en: A hazard is something which could be dangerous to you, your health or safety, or your plans or reputation.

words.ex: My grandmother gave me the heirloom necklace.
words.ex_cn: 奶奶把这串祖传的项链给了我。
words.en: An heirloom is a valuable object that has belonged to a family for several generations.

words.tr: n. 传家宝；祖传物 (heirloom的复数形式)
words.ex: She keeps her grandmother's heirlooms in a wooden box.
words.ex_cn: 她把祖母的传家宝放在一个木箱里。
words.en: An heirloom is a valuable object that has belonged to a family for several generations.

words.ex: He inherited his family's heritage.
words.ex_cn: 他继承了家族的遗产。
words.en: Heritage refers to the traditions, achievements, beliefs, etc., that are part of the history of a group or nation.

words.ex: The historian wrote a book about ancient Rome.
words.ex_cn: 这位历史学家写了一本关于古罗马的书。
words.en: A historian is a person who studies or writes about history; an expert in history.

words.tr: v. 搭便车旅游；沿途搭乘别人车旅行
words.ex: He wants to hitchhike across the country.
words.ex_cn: 他想搭便车横跨全国。
words.en: To travel by getting free rides from passing vehicles.

words.ex: The robbers took a hostage during the bank robbery.
words.ex_cn: 劫匪在银行抢劫时抓了一名人质。
words.en: A hostage is someone who has been captured by a person or organization and who may be killed or injured if people do not do what that person or organization demands.

words.tr: n. 人性；人类；人道；仁慈；
words.ex: Kindness shows the best of humanity.
words.ex_cn: 善良展现了人性中最美好的一面。
words.en: Humanity refers to all human beings collectively or the qualities that make us human, such as kindness, compassion, and the ability to reason.

words.tr:
adj. 被羞辱的
v. 使屈辱；使丢脸；使蒙羞；“humiliate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He felt humiliated when he failed the test in front of everyone.
words.ex_cn: 当他当着大家的面考试失败时，他感到羞辱。
words.en: Feeling ashamed or foolish because you have been made to look weak, stupid, or ridiculous.

words.tr: adj. 羞辱性的；丢脸的； v. “humiliate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The humiliating comment made him feel small.
words.ex_cn: 那句羞辱性的话让他感到自己很渺小。
words.en: If something is humiliating, it makes you feel ashamed and stupid, often because it involves a loss of respect or dignity in front of other people.

words.ex: He tells humorous stories that make everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他讲一些幽默的故事，让大家都笑。
words.en: If you are humorous, you are able to be amusing and to make people laugh.

words.ex: The scientist studies hybridization between two plant species.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家研究两种植物之间的杂交。
words.en: The process of combining different varieties or species to create a hybrid.

words.ex: He entered a deep hypnosis during the therapy.
words.ex_cn: 他在治疗过程中进入了深度催眠状态。
words.en: Hypnosis is a state in which a person seems to be asleep but can still see, hear, or respond to things said to them.

words.ex: He is hypocritical when he says he hates lying but lies all the time.
words.ex_cn: 他说他讨厌撒谎，却总是撒谎，这很虚伪。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being hypocritical, you mean that they pretend to have qualities, beliefs, or feelings that they do not really have.

words.ex: It is a hypothetical situation.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个假设的情况。
words.en: A hypothetical situation, idea, or explanation is based on possible ideas or situations rather than actual ones.

words.ex: The two shirts are identical.
words.ex_cn: 这两件衬衫是一样的。
words.en: Exactly the same, or very similar.

words.tr: n. 认同; 鉴定( identification的名词复数 ); 验明; 身份证明
words.ex: The children showed identifications with their favorite heroes.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们表现出对偶像的认同。
words.en: The act of recognizing or naming someone or something, or the fact of being recognized or named.

words.tr:
adj. 文盲的；无知的；
n. 文盲；无知识的人；
words.ex: He is illiterate and cannot read simple signs.
words.ex_cn: 他是文盲，无法阅读简单的标识。
words.en: Someone who is illiterate cannot read or write.

words.ex: The mirror creates an illusion of a bigger room.
words.ex_cn: 镜子制造出房间更大的错觉。
words.en: An illusion is a false idea or belief, especially about yourself or your situation.

words.ex: He is an illustrious scientist who won many awards.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位杰出的科学家，获得过许多奖项。
words.en: If you describe someone as illustrious, you mean that they are very well known because they have a high position in society or they have done something impressive.

words.ex: The child gave an imaginative story about flying cats.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子讲了一个关于会飞的猫的富有想象力的故事。
words.en: If you describe someone or their ideas as imaginative, you are praising them because they are easily able to think of or create new or exciting things.

words.ex: She was immensely happy after winning the prize.
words.ex_cn: 她赢得奖品后极大地开心。
words.en: To an extremely great extent or degree.

words.ex: Immigration to this country has increased recently.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家的移民数量最近增加了。
words.en: Immigration is the act of coming to live permanently in a country that is not your own.

words.ex: The new law gave impetus to environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 新法律为环境保护提供了推动力。
words.en: Something that gives a process impetus or an impetus makes it happen or progress more quickly.

words.ex: The government will implement new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将实施新规定。
words.en: To implement something means to ensure that what has been planned is done.

words.ex: The implementation of the new rule took one month.
words.ex_cn: 新规则的履行花了一个月。
words.en: The act of putting a decision or plan into effect; execution.

words.ex: His silence was an implicit apology.
words.ex_cn: 他的沉默是一种含蓄的道歉。
words.en: Something that is implicit is expressed in an indirect way.

words.ex: He faced imprisonment for stealing money.
words.ex_cn: 他因偷钱而面临监禁。
words.en: The state of being confined in prison; the act of putting someone in prison or the condition of being kept in prison.

words.tr: adj. 凭冲动行事的；易冲动的
words.ex: He made an impulsive decision to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他一时冲动决定辞掉工作。
words.en: If you describe someone as impulsive, you mean that they do things suddenly without thinking about them carefully first.

words.ex: Wearing shorts to the meeting is inappropriate.
words.ex_cn: 穿短裤去参加会议是不合适的。
words.en: If you say that something is inappropriate, you are criticizing it because you think it is not suitable for a particular situation or purpose.

words.tr: n. 诱因；动机；激励某人做某事的事物；激励某人做某事的事物( incentive的名词复数 )；
words.ex: The company offers incentives for employees who work overtime.
words.ex_cn: 公司为加班的员工提供诱因。
words.en: Something that motivates or encourages someone to do something or to work harder.

words.tr: adj. 倾向于…的； v. “incline”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is inclined to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他倾向于帮助别人。
words.en: Having a tendency or preference towards something; likely to do or be something.

words.ex: It is inconceivable that he forgot his own birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他忘了自己生日，这简直难以想象。
words.en: If something is inconceivable, it is impossible to imagine or believe because it is so unlikely.

words.tr: adj. 不为别人着想的；不体谅别人的；
words.ex: He left the door open and didn't care about others.
words.ex_cn: 他让门敞着，一点也不为别人着想。
words.en: If you describe someone as inconsiderate, you are criticizing them because they do not take enough care over how their words or actions will affect other people.

words.ex: The movie was incredibly funny.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影极其搞笑。
words.en: In a manner that is difficult to believe; extremely.

words.tr: adj. 不感兴趣的；不关心的；
words.ex: He was indifferent to the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影不感兴趣。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being indifferent to something, you mean that they have a complete lack of interest in it.

words.ex: He is an industrious student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤勉的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is industrious works hard and is determined.

words.ex: The mushrooms are inedible and dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 这些蘑菇不能吃，而且危险。
words.en: If something is inedible, it is not suitable for eating because it is unpleasant or harmful.

words.ex: He will inevitably fail if he doesn't study.
words.ex_cn: 如果他不学习，他不可避免地会失败。
words.en: If something will inevitably happen, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

words.ex: He is inexperienced in managing teams.
words.ex_cn: 他在管理团队方面没有经验。
words.en: If you describe someone as inexperienced, you mean that they have little knowledge or experience of a particular situation or activity.

words.tr: adj. 无法解释的；费解的
words.ex: His sudden silence was inexplicable.
words.ex_cn: 他突然的沉默无法解释。
words.en: If something is inexplicable, you cannot explain why it happens or why it is true.

words.ex: The influencer posts photos every day.
words.ex_cn: 这位网红每天发布照片。
words.en: An influencer is a person who has the power to affect the purchasing decisions of others because of his or her authority, knowledge, position, or relationship with his or her audience.

words.tr: adj. 增进知识的；提供消息的；
words.ex: The documentary is very informative.
words.ex_cn: 这部纪录片非常增进了知识。
words.en: Providing useful or interesting information.

words.ex: The inhabitant lives in a small house.
words.ex_cn: 这位居民住在一所小房子里。
words.en: An inhabitant of a place is one of the people who live there.

words.tr: v. 吸入( inhale的现在分词 )
words.ex: He is inhaling deeply before he speaks.
words.ex_cn: 他在说话前深吸一口气。
words.en: To breathe in air, smoke, or gas.

words.ex: He received his father's watch as an inheritance.
words.ex_cn: 他收到了父亲留给他的手表作为遗产。
words.en: Inheritance is money or property which you receive from someone who has died.

words.tr: n. 含沙射影; 暗讽; 讽刺的话; 影射的话( innuendo的名词复数 )
words.ex: He made some innuendos about his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他对他的老板说了些暗示性的话。
words.en: An indirect or subtle, usually derogatory implication in expression; an insinuation.

words.tr: adj. 疯狂的；精神失常的；精神错乱的
words.ex: He thinks it's insane to drive without a license.
words.ex_cn: 他认为无证驾驶是疯狂的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as insane, you mean that they are very foolish or crazy.

words.tr: adj. 漠不关心的；懵然不知的；感觉迟钝的
words.ex: He was insensitive to her feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的感受漠不关心。
words.en: If you describe someone as insensitive, you are criticizing them for being unaware of or unsympathetic to other people's feelings.

words.tr: n. 检查员；巡视员；视察员；
words.ex: The inspector checked the building for safety.
words.ex_cn: 检查员检查了建筑物的安全性。
words.en: An inspector is a person whose job is to inspect something.

words.tr: n. 不足，不充分；机能不全；不适当
words.ex: The insufficiency of water caused the plants to die.
words.ex_cn: 水的不足导致植物死亡。
words.en: If there is an insufficiency of something, there is not enough of it for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He bought insurance for his car.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的车买了保险。
words.en: Insurance is an arrangement in which you pay money to a company, and they pay money to you if something unpleasant happens to you, for example if your property is stolen or damaged, or if you get a serious illness.

words.ex: The integration of technology and education improves learning.
words.ex_cn: 技术与教育的结合改善了学习。
words.en: The act or process of combining or adding parts to make a unified whole.

words.ex: His intellect helps him solve difficult problems.
words.ex_cn: 他的智力帮助他解决难题。
words.en: The ability to understand and think in a logical way about things.

words.ex: He is intellectually curious about science.
words.ex_cn: 他在智力上对科学充满好奇。
words.en: In a way that relates to the intellect or is characterized by intellectual activity.

words.ex: He worked intensely to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他强烈地工作以完成这个项目。
words.en: If something is intense, it is very great or extreme in strength or degree.

words.tr: v. 连结；连结( interlink的现在分词 )；
words.ex: The roads interlinking the villages make travel easier.
words.ex_cn: 连接村庄的道路使出行更方便。
words.en: To connect or link together in a way that allows mutual interaction or influence.

words.tr: n. 间歇；暂停；中间休息
words.ex: There is a ten-minute intermission during the play.
words.ex_cn: 这场戏中间有十分钟的中场休息。
words.en: An intermission is a short break between parts of a play, film, concert, or other performance.

words.tr: v. 阻碍( intervene的第三人称单数 ); 出面; 插嘴; 介于…之间
words.ex: He intervenes when the two boys fight.
words.ex_cn: 当两个男孩打架时，他出面阻止。
words.en: If you intervene in a situation, you become involved in it and try to change it.

words.ex: The teacher made an intervention to help the student.
words.ex_cn: 老师进行了干预以帮助学生。
words.en: Intervention is the act of intervening, especially in a situation to prevent something undesirable from happening.

words.ex: He is intolerant of people who are late.
words.ex_cn: 他不能容忍迟到的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as intolerant, you mean that they do not accept behavior and opinions that are different from their own.

words.ex: The bird sang intransitively.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟唱了，没有宾语。
words.en: An intransitive verb is a verb that does not take a direct object.

words.tr: adj. 感兴趣的；策划阴谋（intrigue 的过去式和过...； v. 引起……的兴趣；
words.ex: I was intrigued by the strange story.
words.ex_cn: 我对这个奇怪的故事感到感兴趣。
words.en: If you are intrigued by something, it interests you a lot because it seems strange or mysterious.

words.tr: n. 密谋策划( intrigue的名词复数 ); 神秘气氛; 引人入胜的复杂情节 v. 搞阴谋诡计
words.ex: The politicians were involved in many intrigues to gain power.
words.ex_cn: 这些政客卷入了众多密谋策划以获取权力。
words.en: If something intrigues you, it interests you a lot because it seems strange or mysterious.

words.tr: adj. 引起兴趣的；引人入胜的； v. “intrigue”的现在分词；
words.ex: The mystery story was intriguing.
words.ex_cn: 这个侦探故事很引人入胜。
words.en: If you describe something as intriguing, you mean that it is interesting or strange.

words.tr: adj. 固有的；内在的；本身的；
words.ex: Honesty is an intrinsic part of her character.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是她性格中固有的部分。
words.en: belonging to a thing by its very nature

words.tr: n. 内向的人；不喜欢与人交往的人
words.ex: He is an introvert who likes reading alone.
words.ex_cn: 他是个喜欢独自读书的内向者。
words.en: An introvert is a person who tends to shrink from social contacts and to become preoccupied with their own thoughts.

words.ex: He is invariably late for meetings.
words.ex_cn: 他总是开会迟到。
words.en: If something invariably happens or is invariably true, it always happens or is always true.

words.ex: The police started an investigation into the accident.
words.ex_cn: 警方对这起事故展开了调查。
words.en: An investigation is a careful search or examination in order to discover facts or information.

words.ex: It's an irony that the fire station burned down.
words.ex_cn: 消防站着火了，这真是讽刺。
words.en: Irony is a subtle form of humor which involves saying things that you do not mean.

words.tr: adj. 不能赎回的；不能兑现的；不可救药的
words.ex: The bond is irredeemable and will never be paid back.
words.ex_cn: 这种债券是不能赎回的，永远不会被偿还。
words.en: If you describe something as irredeemable, you mean that it is so bad or undesirable that there is no way to improve it or make it acceptable.

words.tr: adv. 无法抵抗地，不能自持地; 极为诱惑人地
words.ex: The cake looked irresistibly delicious.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕看起来诱人极了。
words.en: In a manner that is impossible to resist; very attractively.

words.ex: The damage to the environment is irreversible.
words.ex_cn: 对环境的破坏是不可逆转的。
words.en: If a change is irreversible, it cannot be changed back to how it was before.

words.ex: The irritation on his arm hurt when he touched it.
words.ex_cn: 他手臂上的疼痛处一碰就疼。
words.en: Irritation is the feeling of annoyance, especially when something keeps happening that you do not like.

words.ex: He felt isolation after moving to a new city.
words.ex_cn: 他搬到新城市后感到孤立。
words.en: The state of being in a place or situation that is separate from others

words.tr:
n. 痒；渴望
v. （使）痒；渴望
words.ex: The mosquito bite caused an itchy on my arm.
words.ex_cn: 蚊子叮咬让我的手臂发痒。
words.en: If you have an itch, you have an unpleasant feeling on your skin that makes you want to scratch. If you itch to do something, you are very eager or impatient to do it.

words.tr: v. 列出清单( itemize的过去式和过去分词 )
words.ex: He gave an itemized list of his expenses.
words.ex_cn: 他提供了一份详细的开支清单。
words.en: If you itemize a number of things, you make a list of them.

words.ex: We planned our itinerary before the trip.
words.ex_cn: 我们在旅行前规划了路线。
words.en: An itinerary is a plan of a journey, including the route and the places that you will visit.

words.tr: v. 歪曲( juggle的过去式和过去分词 ); 耍弄; 有效地组织; 尽力同时应付（两个或两个以
words.ex: He juggled the facts to make himself look better.
words.ex_cn: 他歪曲了事实，让自己看起来更好。
words.en: To juggle means to keep several objects in motion in the air at the same time by alternately throwing and catching them. It can also mean to deal with several things at the same time, often in a way that is not entirely honest or fair.

words.tr: n. 玩杂耍的人; 杂耍，把戏
words.ex: The juggler throws three balls in the air.
words.ex_cn: 杂技演员在空中抛三个球。
words.en: A juggler is someone who entertains people by juggling objects such as balls, plates, or knives, often as part of a performance.

words.tr:
adj. 青少年的；幼稚的；
n. 少年；
words.ex: The book is written for juvenile readers.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是为青少年读者撰写的。
words.en: A juvenile is a child or young person who is not yet old enough to be considered an adult.

words.tr: v. 踢； n. 极度兴奋；（毒品或酒精的）效力( kick的名词复数 )；
words.ex: He kicks the ball hard.
words.ex_cn: 他用力踢球。
words.en: To strike out with the foot or feet; to make a sudden forceful thrust with the foot.

words.ex: She knit a warm scarf for her brother.
words.ex_cn: 她为她的弟弟织了一条暖和的围巾。
words.en: If you knit something, especially an article of clothing, you make it from wool or a similar thread by using two knitting needles or a machine.

words.ex: He works in a laboratory on Fridays.
words.ex_cn: 他在星期五去实验室工作。
words.en: A laboratory is a place equipped for scientific research, experiments, or teaching.

words.ex: His laziness made him miss the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他的懒惰让他错过了公交车。
words.en: The state of being unwilling to work or use energy; idleness.

words.tr: n. 领导才能；领导地位；
words.ex: His leadership helped the team win the match.
words.ex_cn: 他的领导才能帮助团队赢得了比赛。
words.en: Leadership is the ability to lead, guide, or direct a group, organization, or country.

words.ex: He hired a legal lawyer to help him.
words.ex_cn: 他请了一位法律律师来帮助他。
words.en: Relating to the law or to lawyers, or permitted or required by law.

words.ex: He is a legendary basketball player.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位传奇的篮球运动员。
words.en: Something or someone that is legendary is very famous and is often talked about in a way that suggests they are almost mythical.

words.tr: adj. 合法的；法律认可的；合理的；
words.ex: This contract is legitimate and signed by both parties.
words.ex_cn: 这份合同是合法的，并由双方签署。
words.en: Something that is legitimate is acceptable according to the law.

words.ex: He legitimately won the prize by following all the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他通过遵守所有规则正当地赢得了奖品。
words.en: In a manner that is conforming to the law or to rules.

words.tr: adj. 宽厚的；仁慈的；不严格的；
words.ex: The teacher was lenient with students who were late.
words.ex_cn: 老师对迟到的学生很宽厚。
words.en: If you are lenient with someone, you are not strict in the way you treat them, especially when they have done something wrong.

words.ex: He has a lifelong love for reading.
words.ex_cn: 他对阅读有着终身的热爱。
words.en: Lasting or continuing through all or much of one's life.

words.ex: He lingered by the door, not wanting to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他逗留在门口，不想离开。
words.en: If you linger somewhere, you stay there for a longer time than is necessary, for example because you are enjoying yourself.

words.ex: He turned the loft into a bedroom.
words.ex_cn: 他把阁楼改成了卧室。
words.en: A loft is a room or space directly under the roof of a building, used for accommodation or storage.

words.ex: Eating healthy food helps with longevity.
words.ex_cn: 健康饮食有助于长寿。
words.en: Longevity refers to the length or duration of an individual's life, especially when it is unusually long.

words.tr: adj. 赚大钱的；获利多的；
words.ex: He took a lucrative job at a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他去了一家科技公司做一份赚大钱的工作。
words.en: A lucrative activity or job is one that you can earn a lot of money from.

words.ex: The factory buys lumber to make furniture.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂购买木材来制造家具。
words.en: Lumber refers to wood that has been processed into beams and planks, a stage in the process of wood production. It is also used to describe the action of moving in a slow, heavy, awkward way.

words.ex: He ate a lump of sugar.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一块糖。
words.en: A lump is a solid piece of something, often with no particular shape. If you lump things together, you put them together in a group or treat them as the same.

words.tr:
v. 吸引；诱惑；引诱
n. 诱惑；诱饵；吸引力
words.ex: The bright colors lure the birds to the feeder.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的颜色吸引鸟类来到喂食器。
words.en: If you lure someone, you tempt them to do something or to go somewhere, especially by offering some form of reward.

words.ex: She stayed in a luxurious hotel with gold faucets.
words.ex_cn: 她住进了一家有金色水龙头的奢侈酒店。
words.en: Something that is luxurious is very comfortable and expensive, and often involves great pleasure or indulgence.

words.ex: I love the lyrics of this song.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢这首歌的歌词。
words.en: The words of a song, especially a pop song.

words.ex: The sunset over the mountains was magnificent.
words.ex_cn: 山上的日落壮丽极了。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is magnificent, you mean that you think they are extremely good, beautiful, or impressive.

words.ex: Pop music is part of the mainstream.
words.ex_cn: 流行音乐是主流的一部分。
words.en: The ideas, attitudes, or activities that are shared by most people and regarded as normal or conventional.

words.ex: The cost of maintenance is low for this car.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的维持费用很低。
words.en: The process of preserving a condition or situation or the state of being preserved.

words.ex: The manufacturer makes cars in this factory.
words.ex_cn: 这家制造商在这家工厂生产汽车。
words.en: A manufacturer is a person or company that produces goods in large quantities, especially in a factory.

words.tr: adj. 边缘的；页边的；微不足道的；不重要的
words.ex: The village is on the marginal area of the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于城市的边缘地区。
words.en: If you describe something as marginal, you mean that it is small or not very important.

words.ex: The view from the mountain is marvelous.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色极好。
words.en: If you describe something as marvelous, you are emphasizing that it is extremely good.

words.ex: He put a mat on the floor to keep it clean.
words.ex_cn: 他在地上放了一块垫子以保持清洁。
words.en: A mat is a piece of thick fabric or other material that is placed on a floor or other surface to protect it or to provide a soft surface to stand or sit on.

words.ex: The mechanical toy moves with batteries.
words.ex_cn: 这个机械玩具用电池驱动。
words.en: Relating to machines or machinery; operated by or involving a machine or machines.

words.ex: The body has a mechanism to fight viruses.
words.ex_cn: 人体有一种对抗病毒的机制。
words.en: A mechanism is a part of a machine that does a particular task, or a system that is intended to achieve something or deal with a problem.

words.tr: n. 药物；药物治疗；药物处理；
words.ex: He took his medication every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃药。
words.en: Medication refers to a substance used for medical treatment, especially a medicine or drug.

words.ex: The castle is a medieval building.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡是一座中世纪的建筑。
words.en: Relating to the Middle Ages, the period in European history from about the 5th century to the 15th century.

words.ex: The movie was mediocre and not worth watching.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很平庸，不值得看。
words.en: If you describe something as mediocre, you mean that it is of average quality but you think it should be better.

words.ex: He refused to accept mediocrity in his work.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝在工作中接受平凡。
words.en: If you refer to the mediocrity of something, you mean that it is of average quality but you think it should be better.

words.tr:
adj. 微型的；
n. 微型画；小型模型；
words.ex: He bought a miniature car for his collection.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的收藏买了一辆微型汽车。
words.en: A miniature is a very small detailed painting, often a portrait. It can also refer to a small-scale model or representation of something.

words.tr: v. 行为不端；行为无礼貌
words.ex: The boy misbehaved in class.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩在课堂上行为不端。
words.en: If someone, especially a child, misbehaves, they behave in a way that is not acceptable to other people.

words.ex: He misinformed the crowd about the time.
words.ex_cn: 他告诉人群错误的时间。
words.en: To misinform someone means to give them false or inaccurate information.

words.ex: He eats sweets with moderation.
words.ex_cn: 他吃甜食很适度。
words.en: Moderation is the quality of doing something within reasonable limits; not too much or too little.

words.ex: He will modify the plan tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会更改计划。
words.en: To change something slightly, especially in order to make it more suitable for a particular purpose.

words.tr: n. （由鼹鼠打洞扒出的泥土堆成的）鼹鼠丘；琐事；无意义的事；小困难（或障碍）
words.ex: The dog dug up a molehill in the backyard.
words.ex_cn: 狗在后院挖了一个鼹鼠丘。
words.en: A molehill is a small mound of earth thrown up by a mole burrowing near the surface.

words.ex: The team gained momentum after scoring the first goal.
words.ex_cn: 球队在进第一个球后获得了势头。
words.en: Momentum is the ability of something to keep increasing, developing, or being more successful.

words.ex: The team's morale improved after they won the game.
words.ex_cn: 球队赢了比赛后，士气提升了。
words.en: Morale is the amount of confidence and cheerfulness that a group of people have.

words.ex: The mortality rate in the region increased last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年该地区的死亡率上升了。
words.en: Mortality refers to the state of being subject to death or the number of deaths in a particular population or period.

words.ex: The motorist stopped at the red light.
words.ex_cn: 这位驾车者在红灯前停下了车。
words.en: A motorist is a person who drives a car.

words.tr:
v. 咕哝；含糊地说
n. 含糊的话；咕哝
words.ex: He mumbles when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，他会嘟囔。
words.en: If you mumble, you speak very quietly and not at all clearly with the result that the words are difficult to understand.

words.tr:
n. 低语声；嘟哝
v. 低语；咕哝；私下抱怨
words.ex: I heard a murmur from the next room.
words.ex_cn: 我听到隔壁房间传来低语声。
words.en: A murmur is a low, indistinct, continuous sound, as of a stream or of voices.

words.ex: He has a small mustache.
words.ex_cn: 他有一小撮胡子。
words.en: A mustache is a strip of hair left to grow above the upper lip.

words.ex: The mysterious box appeared on his doorstep.
words.ex_cn: 那个神秘的盒子出现在他的门口。
words.en: If someone or something is mysterious, it is not fully understood or explained and seems interesting or puzzling.

words.ex: He put on a blue necktie for the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他为面试戴了一条蓝色领带。
words.en: A necktie is a long piece of cloth that is worn around the neck, usually by men, and is tied in a knot at the front. Neckties are often worn as part of formal or business attire.

words.tr: adj. 疏忽的；粗心的；不在意的
words.ex: He was negligent in doing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他做作业时很疏忽。
words.en: If you say that someone is negligent, you mean that they do not take enough care over something that they are responsible for.

words.tr: n. [解剖]神经；神经紧张；胆量（nerve 的复数）；
words.ex: The nerves in his hand sent pain signals to his brain.
words.ex_cn: 他手里的神经向大脑传递了疼痛信号。
words.en: Nerves are the fibers that carry messages between your brain and other parts of your body, allowing you to move and feel things. They can also refer to feelings of worry or anxiety about something that is going to happen.

words.ex: It was raining, nonetheless, we went for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 天下着雨，尽管如此，我们还是去散步了。
words.en: Nonetheless is used to indicate that something is true or happens in spite of what has just been said.

words.ex: The data shows normality after the transformation.
words.ex_cn: 经过转换后，数据呈现出正态性。
words.en: Normality is a situation in which everything is normal.

words.ex: He felt nostalgic when he saw his old toy.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到自己的旧玩具时，他感到怀旧。
words.en: If you feel nostalgic, you feel both happy and slightly sad when you think about things that happened in the past.

words.tr: adj. 声名狼藉的；臭名昭著的；
words.ex: He is a notorious thief who stole from many stores.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个声名狼藉的小偷，偷过许多商店。
words.en: Someone or something that is notorious is well known for something bad.

words.ex: The toy store sells many novelty items for children.
words.ex_cn: 玩具店出售许多为儿童设计的新奇物品。
words.en: The quality of being new, original, or unusual; something new, original, or unusual.

words.ex: He eats nuts every morning for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃坚果当早餐。
words.en: If you say that someone is nuts, you mean that they are crazy. Nuts are hard-shelled fruits of some trees.

words.ex: Obesity is a serious health problem in many countries.
words.ex_cn: 肥胖是许多国家的一个严重健康问题。
words.en: Obesity is a medical condition in which excess body fat has accumulated to the extent that it may have a negative effect on health.

words.ex: He felt an obligation to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他感到有义务帮助他的朋友。
words.en: An obligation is something that you must do because you have promised, because of a law, etc.

words.ex: The obscene behavior shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这种可憎的行为让所有人都震惊了。
words.en: If you describe something as obscene, you mean it offends you because it relates to sex or violence in a way that you think is unpleasant and shocking.

words.ex: The rotten food has a bad odor.
words.ex_cn: 腐烂的食物有一种难闻的气味。
words.en: An odor is a particular and distinctive smell.

words.ex: The dogs had three offspring last spring.
words.ex_cn: 这些狗去年春天生了三只幼崽。
words.en: Someone's offspring are their children.

words.ex: The operator answered the phone quickly.
words.ex_cn: 接线员迅速接听了电话。
words.en: An operator is a person who operates equipment or a machine, or a person who is in charge of a telephone switchboard.

words.ex: He is an optimist who believes things will get better.
words.ex_cn: 他是个乐观主义者，相信事情会好转。
words.en: An optimist is someone who always expects good things to happen or is always hopeful about the future.

words.tr: n. 入学介绍；岗前训练；方向；取向；
words.ex: The school held an orientation for new students on Monday.
words.ex_cn: 学校在周一为新生举行了入学介绍。
words.en: The act of orienting or the state of being oriented; the determination of the relative position of something or someone (especially oneself).

words.ex: The building has beautiful ornamentation on its walls.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑的墙壁上有精美的装饰。
words.en: The act of decorating or the state of being decorated, especially in architecture and the decorative arts.

words.tr: n. 孤儿；失去生母的幼小动物
words.ex: The boy lives with his uncle because he is an orphan.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩和叔叔住在一起，因为他是个孤儿。
words.en: An orphan is a child whose parents are dead.

words.tr: n. 出口；发泄途径；经销店；折扣店
words.ex: The river flows out through an outlet.
words.ex_cn: 河水通过一个出口流出。
words.en: An outlet is a hole or pipe through which liquid or air can flow out, or a point in a wall where you can connect electrical equipment to the electricity supply.

words.ex: There was an outpouring of love after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，人们倾注了满满的爱。
words.en: An outpouring is a very strong expression of feeling or emotion that is expressed openly and often in large amounts.

words.ex: The unfair verdict caused public outrage.
words.ex_cn: 不公正的判决引发了公众的愤怒。
words.en: An outrage is an extremely strong reaction of anger, shock, or indignation.

words.ex: He overestimated his ability to finish the task in one day.
words.ex_cn: 他过高估计了自己一天内完成任务的能力。
